description:
We are STEM students from Sharkya STEM School, A team on a mission to code a solution that makes data accessible to everyone.

We have observed that Earth data is limited to visual forms, preventing approximately 2.2 million people from experiencing and understanding Earth’s changes. So we decided to empower them to See Earth Through Sound.
summary:
Terra Tone turns NASA Earth data into sound, so people can hear how our planet is changing. Most climate data is shared through charts and maps, which leaves out people who are blind or have low vision. We wanted a way for everyone to experience the same science.
The journey begins with the Terra Tone game. Terra guides players through nine sound missions to restore air, water and soil, comparing pollution signals by ear, with narration, Arabic and English voice commands and keyboard control. A moon-orbit transition then opens the Terra-Tone Explorer, where any location's NASA POWER climate history plays as music: the higher the value, the higher the pitch. Users can compare two cities in stereo, explore aerosols, ozone and carbon monoxide through NASA GIBS and SVS visuals synchronized with graphs, read trend statistics and turn their own image into sound.
We built the website with React, Vite, the Web Audio API, Chart.js and Leaflet, hosted on GitHub Pages, and the game with HTML and JavaScript, plus a Godot version. Automated tests verify our statistics, and uploaded images never leave the user's device.
Our creativity lies in letting players hear pollution before reading about it, where data becomes melody and two cities become a stereo duet. We separated real NASA data from labelled simulations, kept sound mappings simple, made everything bilingual, and remembered that a sound shows change, not its cause
